findings.title: Jobs 1 and 2 can be logged as successes without the lessons they exist to teach: no filter in job 1, one capacitor in job 2, so the LC and DC-latch ideas can be skipped completely
findings.problem:
A job advances on any verdict of tier 1 or higher (station.ts:194-199). Tier 1 means only 'S/N ≥ 6 dB' (logic.ts:176). I played a shortcut run (mockups/review5/tools/observatory-teach/b.mjs), and the room was finished in about 10 actions without using any of the electronics:
(1) Job 1 'Clean up the garbled message': move the cart about 7 m, flip the ROUTE lever and log, with no filter can at all. S/N was 10.7 dB, tier 1, the toast said 'Decodes', and the job advanced (shot 11). The filter lesson (shunt capacitor, corner frequency below the 9 kHz noise) is optional.
(2) Job 2 'Keep the shutter latch powered': put one capacitor in SHUNT and turn it up to 3.3 µF. S/N 7.1 dB, tier 1, job advanced (shot 12). The same happens at 4.7 and 6.8 µF, and with small-R RC pairs: 24 RC combinations and 3 single-C values all reach tier 1 (numbers from n2.mjs). PROGRESS.md:333-335 says 'Job 2 needs a steeper filter … no single part at any value decodes reliably'. That is true only for the 12 dB 'reliable' bar, and even then by 0.1 dB (the best single C gives 11.9 dB). The 'decodes' bar lets it through.
(3) A shunt capacitor never touches the DC path, so the player who takes this route never sees the latch drop out. The one DC lesson (a series C blocks steady DC, a series R divides it) only appears to a player who happens to try a series C or R.
(4) Job 3 then inherits the same one-capacitor filter, and needs only rod + orient.
The result card for this run reads A / A / A (shot 18), the same as a fully elegant run (shot 37). So the player who learned nothing and the one who built a proper LC filter get the same grade; only three 9-px bonus stars differ. This breaks DR-26 (the concept must decide success), DR-38 (tiers must reward understanding) and DR-07. It also undercuts the room's whole teaching arc: the LC filter, the inductor carrying DC, and the series-C trap all become optional reading.
findings.fix:
Make the concept the gate.
(a) In station.ts 'log', treat tier 1 as a near-miss that does not advance the job and is not a mistake. Toast: 'It decodes, but the next gust of noise will garble it: 7 dB is not enough margin.' Keep the job open. Alternatively, keep tier 1 advancing in jobs 1 and 3, but in job 2 have JOBS[1] require tier ≥ 2 (add `minTier:2` to the Job interface).
(b) Retune so single parts truly fail job 2's DECODE bar, not just the reliable bar. For example raise the job-2 whine to brush(4000,2.2,4), or raise SPEC.decodeSnr for job 2 to 9 dB. Then extend the unit test at logic.test.ts:292-295 to `toBe(0)` for every single can.
(c) Make the DC latch unavoidable: start job 2 with the shunt slot cleared and a SERIES resistor already fitted 'from the last engineer' (series R 470 Ω, so latch 6.4 V and the lamp is out). The player then meets the dropped latch first and must replace the series part, which teaches 'what goes in series must carry DC'.
(d) Grade on it: see the grading finding.
findings.verify: Unit test: for job 'latch', judge(single can any value).tier===0. New station spec 'observatory: a single capacitor does not finish job 2' (act pick C, slot shunt, value 3.3e-6, log → station.job stays 1). Re-run mockups/review5/tools/observatory-teach/b.mjs: the run must not reach won, and shot 12 must show the job still open.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it in mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/v1.mjs. I moved the cart 7.1 m, flipped the route and logged with no can: S/N 10.7, tier 1, toast 'Decodes', and the job advanced (station.ts:194-199). In job 2 a single 3.3 µF shunt gave 7.1 dB, tier 1, and the job advanced. Job 3 then needed only the rod. The run was won with logged tiers [1,1,1] and the card read A/A/A (verify-observatory-teach-06-result-card.jpg), the same as the reviewer's tier-3 run (observatory-teach-37). Some details in the finding are wrong. (a) The best single part in job 2 gives 10.1 dB (6.8 µF shunt), not 11.9; PROGRESS.md:333-335 also says 10.1. It fails the reliable bar by 1.9 dB, not 0.1. (b) 22 RC pairs reach tier 1, not 24. (c) The unit test it cites is at logic.test.ts:98-101, not 292-295; the file has 106 lines. Fix (b) is technically wrong as written. With the whine at brush(4000,2.2,4), the intended 10 mH + 1 µF answer drops to 8.2 dB, tier 1, which breaks logic.test.ts:60, and one single part still decodes.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/num.mjs output: j2 single shunt C tier 1 at 3.3/4.7/6.8 µF (7.1/8.8/10.1 dB); best single part 10.1 dB; RC tier>0 = 22

Even with a tier gate, job 1 is still tier 3 with no cans when the cart is ≥10 m away and the route is flipped (num.mjs: d=10 rr → 12.7 dB, tier 3), so the filter stays optional unless the finding-11 distance cap is also applied
findings.fix_correction: Drop option (b) 'raise the whine to 2.2': it pushes the taught 10 mH + 1 µF answer to tier 1. Gate instead. Add `minTier` to Job (job 2: minTier 2). Because logic.test.ts:98-101 already proves that no single part reaches tier 2, this alone makes the LC/DC-latch lesson required. If a decode-bar retune is still wanted, set a per-job decodeSnr of about 10.5 dB for job 2 (the best single part is 10.1 dB) and re-check that the LC solutions stay tier 3. In station.ts 'log', a tier below minTier is a near-miss: no mistake is counted and the job stays open. For job 1, also cap the distance used by judge and solutions at CART_SAFE (see finding 11), or require a can in job 1, so 'far cart + lever' does not skip the filter. Keep (c), the pre-fitted 470 Ω series R: latch = 12·600/1120 = 6.43 V, which is correct.

findings.title: The grade can't tell understanding from luck: a tier-1, one-mistake run gets A on all three axes, and the cost axis rewards using fewer parts than the lesson needs
findings.problem:
The limits are time 360 s, damage 1, and cost = ceil(sum of cheapest reliable costs × 1.25) = ceil(9 × 1.25) = 12 (station.ts:63, :82). grade() takes the best of the three axes (src/sim/grade.ts:3-6).
(1) The shortcut run (no filter, one capacitor, a wrong whip logged once) spent 5–6 credits, under the 12 limit, so cost is A. It made 1 mistake (≤ 1), so damage is A. Time is A. Overall A (shot 18).
(2) The proper run (shunt C, then LC 10 mH + 1 µF, then right whip) spent 7–11 and got the same A/A/A (shot 37).
The cost axis is set from the cheapest *reliable* filter, so under-filtering always looks thrifty. It actively rewards not building the LC. Damage A tolerates one failed log, so the only thing that separates good play is three bonus stars drawn at about 9 px on the result card. This breaks DR-07 ('standing still or pure wrecking can't earn A on all three') and DR-38.
findings.fix: In ObservatoryBench.score(), return a cost that includes a margin penalty: add (2 − tier) × 3 credits per job logged below tier 2 ('the decode will need a re-send'). Equivalently, set limits.cost from the cheapest reliable cost (9, no ×1.25 slack) and charge tier-1 logs. Alternatively, count each tier-1 log as half a mistake in `damage`. Keep damage at 1 but do not count logs made while S/N ≥ decodeSnr (those are near-misses, not damage). On the result card (src/ui/game-ui.ts:217), show which axis earned the grade, per DR-07.
findings.verify: Re-run b.mjs (shortcut) and c.mjs (tier 3). The shortcut's result card must not be A/A/A; the tier-3 run stays A on all three. Add a unit or spec assertion on snapshot().station after the shortcut sequence: score().cost > limits.cost.
findings.verify_reason: limits = {time:360, damage:1, cost: ceil((1+4+4)×1.25) = 12} (station.ts:63, :82; num.mjs prints a limit cost of 12). My shortcut run had logged tiers [1,1,1], 1 mistake and cost 5 on the card (spent 6), and got A/A/A (verify-observatory-teach-06). The reviewer's tier-3 run got A/A/A with cost 7 (observatory-teach-37). The only difference is the three tiny bonus stars. The finding is right that grade() takes the BEST axis (grade.ts:6: [...parts].sort()[0] puts 'A' first). That matters for the fix: making the cost axis B alone would still leave overall A.
extra_evidence: src/sim/grade.ts:6 overall = best of three axes
findings.fix_correction: The cost or damage change is fine, but note that grade() returns the best axis. Per-axis letters will change, but any 'overall' readout stays A while time is A. Either add tier-weighted damage (count each tier-1 log as a mistake, limit 1 → B at 2), or have the room's result use the worst of the axes, or require bonus 1 for an A on the cost axis. The verify step should check per-axis letters, not overall.

findings.title: The 'shutter latch' and the 'dome motor' don't exist in the world: job 2's noise source and its failure consequence are invisible
findings.problem:
Job 2 reads 'Keep the shutter latch powered … The dome motor whines at 4 kHz' (logic.ts:124-125). Job 3's message is 'DOME OPEN'. But room.ts:67-79 builds the dome as a static half-shell with a telescope. There is no shutter, no dome motor and no slit that opens (shots 43, 01). The noise in jobs 2 and 3 therefore has no physical source the player can see, hear in the room or move (logic.ts:141: 'reaches the receiver through its own mount').
When the latch drops out (series C or series R logged), the only consequence in the world is a 4 cm lamp on the board turning from green to dark (station.ts:125, :239; shot 25), plus the sentence in the toast. Nothing slams, nothing closes, the telescope doesn't move. DR-28 asks that failure show its cause in the world first; DR-47 asks that devices show their state; DR-37 says hidden rules must be shown.
The success payoff is just as invisible. 'DOME OPEN' and the final 'STARS CLEAR' only appear as text. The lightUp() glow (room.ts:109) is behind the win push-in camera (shots 36 and 17 frame the bench and gallery, not the dome). The player never sees the circuit do anything physical.
findings.fix:
In room.ts, add a two-leaf shutter on the dome slit: two curved panels on hinges at dx,dz, with a small brass dome-motor housing on the dome rim near the rack that vibrates while jobs 2 and 3 are current (sin jitter 2 mm at 30 Hz) and emits a faint 4 kHz-coloured ring pulse every 0.8 s. Export `setShutter(open:boolean)` from dressObservatory.
In station.ts update(), drive the shutter from read(...).latchOk while job 2 or 3 is current: the latch holds → shutter open; latch drops → the shutter slams shut over 0.25 s with a clunk (a.clatter()) and a dust burst, and the telescope tube tilts down. This happens live as soon as a series C or R is slotted, before LOG, so the failure is seen at the part.
On the win, point the push-in at the dome (the game's winFocus) or call lightUp() and open the shutter fully with the stars brightening inside camera view.
findings.verify: Screenshot: slot series C 1 µF in job 2 → shot within 0.5 s shows the shutter closed and the lamp dark. Slot L 10 mH back → shutter open. Win shot shows the dome with brightened stars and Pip in the centre 70%. Spec: snapshot().station.shutter flips with latchOk.
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:67-79 builds a static open half-shell and a telescope with a fixed tilt. There is no shutter, slit or dome motor (observatory-teach-43). The job-2 noise has no in-world source (logic.ts:141). The win push-in frames the bench, because winFocus() returns station.table when a station exists (game.ts:398), so lightUp() at the dome is off camera (verify-observatory-teach-05-win-push.jpg shows only the bench and the gallery). I lowered it to P2. The latch state IS shown live on the device: redraw() sets the LATCH lamp from read() on every change, before LOG (station.ts:239). It goes dark as soon as a series C is slotted (observatory-teach-25), so DR-47 is met at the bench. What is missing is the story-world cause and the payoff, not the state readout. The finding's '4 cm lamp' is a sphere of radius .042, about 8 cm across.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:350 win() calls lightUp() (dome glow at dx,dz) but the camera pushes in on the bench
findings.fix_correction: The shutter idea is fine. Drop 'this happens live… before LOG' as a new requirement for the lamp, which is already live; add it only for the shutter. For the win shot, give ObservatoryBench a winFocus override (for example the dome at (-6.1,1.6,-5.3)) instead of changing the shared game.ts default for all stations.

findings.title: Cable routing, the room's spatial idea, is a lever on the bench; the receiver cable doesn't exist in the room, and 'past the motor' is physically inconsistent (REGRESSION check: still open since R4A)
findings.problem:
The coupling model measures the motor's distance from the rack at RX (-3.25,-2.45) (room.ts:16, station.ts:314). But the 'route' that halves the noise is a lever on the bench, which swaps between two short red tubes lying on the desktop (station.ts:129-133, :187-188, :233).
In the room there is no cable from the ROOF RECEIVER rack to the bench at all. The bench's red lead starts in mid-air at the desk's left edge (shots 40, 42, 07). So once Pip has carried the motor 7 m away (shot 05), the bench still says 'ROUTE: PAST MOTOR', and flipping a lever 7 m from the motor still gains exactly 6 dB (logic.ts:133). That teaches the wrong causal story: noise pickup depends on where the cable runs relative to the source. Here it depends on a lever, wherever the motor is.
It also leaves AGENTS rule 4 ('the cable is the star') unused in the room where routing a cable away from a noise source is literally the lesson. R4A ('the big miss: cable routing is a bench lever') and NEXT_STEPS.md:26 already raised this; it is still not done.
The noise source itself barely reads: the motor's only cue is a 3-particle spark burst every 0.5–1.1 s (station.ts:316), not visible in any of my room shots (40, 42), and nothing links the cart to the receiver line. The noise is visible only on the bench scope.
findings.fix:
Make the receiver line a real room cable. Enable the rope for this station (src/game.ts:92/104 gate), anchored at the rack (anchor RX, length ~9 m) and ending at the bench RECEIVER jack (level.target). Then replace `rerouted:boolean` in Setup with `routeCoupling = Σ over rope segments of 1.2/max(.3, segmentDistance(segment, cart))`, normalised, so dragging the cable away from the cart, or the cart away from the cable, lowers the noise continuously.
Keep the -6 dB lever only as a fallback (remove it once the rope works). Draw faint expanding rings (radius 0.5→2.5 m, opacity 0.25) from the motor while it runs, and tint the rope segments within 1.5 m of the motor yellow on the bench scope's 'pickup' strip.
If the rope is too large a change for now, at minimum: draw a static floor cable from the rack to the bench, routed past the cart's parking spot, and make the lever's effect scale with cartCoupling (rerouted only helps when the cart is within 3 m of the cable).
findings.verify: Spec: drag the rope around the cart → snapshot().station.reading.snr rises with the rope–cart distance. Shot at the game camera: a cable visibly runs from the ROOF RECEIVER rack to the bench. With the cart 7 m away, toggling the route changes S/N by < 1 dB.
findings.verify_reason: cartCoupling multiplies by 0.5 when rerouted, whatever the distance (logic.ts:133), so the lever gives exactly −6 dB with the cart 7–14 m away (num.mjs: d=7 → 3.6 vs 9.6 dB). The route is two tubes on the desktop, toggled by a lever (station.ts:129-133, :233). In observatory-teach-07 the red lead comes in from the desk's left edge, and observatory-teach-42 shows no cable from the ROOF RECEIVER rack to the bench. For stations the rope, plug and target are hidden and never simulated (game.ts:92, :104). NEXT_STEPS.md:26-27 and PROGRESS.md 'Still to do' list this as open. It is a known open item carried over from R4A (DESIGN_A.md:197), not a regression. I did not verify the claim that the motor sparks are hard to see in room shots; it is minor.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:92 (plug/target/anchor hidden for stations), src/game.ts:104 (simulateCable only when !station)
mockups/review5/shots/observatory-teach-07-bench-view-job1.jpg (lead starts at desk edge; 'ROUTE: PAST MOTOR' with cart 7.1 m away)
docs/PROGRESS.md 'Still to do… the receiver line as the real draggable cable in the room'

findings.title: Per-part corner tags mislead in an LC pair (the coil reads '↓ 11 kHz' while the filter rolls off at 1.6 kHz), and the tag's frequency line is about 6 px tall and unreadable
findings.problem:
Each slotted can shows a value tag. Its second line is the corner that part would set on its own (station.ts:226-229, logic.ts:69-72).
(1) In the intended job-2 answer, 10 mH series L + 1 µF shunt C, the tags and the panel read 'L · low-pass 11 kHz' and 'C · low-pass 3.4 kHz' (shots 30, 31b). The noise is at 4 kHz, above the C corner and below the L corner. The two-part filter actually acts at its resonance f0 = 1/(2π√LC) ≈ 1.6 kHz, peaking +3 dB there and boosting the tone to 'Tone level 111%' (panel, shot 30).
So the numbers the bench puts on the objects predict the wrong thing: by the tags the coil 'does nothing' to 4 kHz noise, yet adding it is what makes the decode reliable. A learner reasoning 'corner must sit below the noise' is misled. The only truthful cue is the lavender |H(f)| curve on the scope, which is correct.
(2) The corner line renders at about 6–7 px cap height at 1440×900. In shots 21b and 31b, '↓ 34 kHz', '↓ 11 kHz' and '↓ 3.4 kHz' are barely legible. So the on-object link between value and frequency (the stated design goal in PROGRESS.md:328-332) mostly lives in the side panel's text (DR-48).
(3) A '↓' next to a frequency can be read as 'passes below' or as 'cuts'. Green versus pink is the only other code.
(4) 'Tone level 111%' is never explained.
findings.fix:
In logic.ts, add `filterCorner(f:Filter)`. When series is L and shunt is C, return f0 = 1/(2π√(L·C)); when series is R and shunt is C, return 1/(2π·(rs+R)∥rl·C); otherwise use the single-part corner. In station.ts redraw, when both slots form a 2-part filter, replace the two per-part corner lines on the scope (station.ts:264-266) with one bold 'LC corner 1.6 kHz' line, and show 'LC ↓1.6 kHz' on a bridge tag between the cans. Keep the per-part corners only when one slot is filled.
In valueTag (station.ts:49-52), render the tag at 256×160 with the corner line at 40 px (not 32), and make the plane .34 m wide, so the corner reads at ≥ 14 px cap height. Replace the '↓/↑' with words: 'cuts above 3.4 kHz' / 'cuts below 245 Hz'.
When the tone gain is above 1.05, add a short scope annotation 'resonance boost' at f0.
findings.verify: Crop the board at 10 mH + 1 µF: one LC corner of about 1.6 kHz is shown, and the text measures ≥ 14 px cap height (DR-48). Unit test: filterCorner({series:L10m,shunt:C1u}) ≈ 1590 Hz ±5 %.
findings.verify_reason: Numbers checked (num.mjs). 10 mH + 1 µF: the per-part corners are 10.5 kHz (L) and 3.45 kHz (C); f0 = 1.59 kHz; |H| peaks at 1.41 (+3 dB) near 1.4 kHz; the gain at 700 Hz is 1.11, which explains 'Tone level 111%'. The tags show '↓ 11 kHz' and '↓ 3.4 kHz' (observatory-teach-31b, -30). The corner line is drawn at 32 px on a 256 px texture over a 0.26 m plane (station.ts:49-52, :226), and in the 1440×900 shots it is roughly 5–6 px tall, below DR-48's 14 px. The '↓/↑' glyph ambiguity is a fair point but subjective.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/observatory-teach-30-step-L10m-C1u.jpg (panel: L low-pass 11 kHz, C 3.4 kHz, Tone 111%)

findings.title: The failure messages print the answer: the antenna failure gives 'λ/4 ≈ 0.75 m', and each job's ask lists the method (move, reroute, filter, fit and orient)
findings.problem:
PROGRESS.md:338-340 says the recipe prompts ('λ/4 = c ÷ f ÷ 4', 'move the cart, reroute the cable…') are gone. They have moved rather than gone:
(1) The job-3 failure toast is 'A 1.5 m whip is far from a quarter wave at 100 MHz (λ = c/f = 3.0 m, so λ/4 ≈ 0.75 m). Most of the signal reflects.' (logic.ts:162-164; shot 15). The rack has a '75 cm' label. One failed LOG gives the exact answer, so the only 'apply c = fλ' moment in the room can be done by reading. The room already has the clue in the world: the RADIO exhibit says 'λ ≈ 3 m, f ≈ 100 MHz, FM radio' (room.ts:32; shot 36). Dividing by 4 is the player's job.
(2) The job asks shown on the bench panel are methods. Job 1: 'Move the cart, reroute the cable, filter the line.' Job 3: 'Fit and orient the right whip.' (logic.ts:122, :126; shot 07). These name the tool and the method (DR-39). The unit test 'failure messages say why, never what to change' (logic.test.ts:296-299) only greps for a few phrases, so it misses both.
findings.fix:
logic.ts:163: change the message to 'A 1.5 m whip is a poor match for 100 MHz: most of the signal reflects back down the line.' Keep the λ maths for a second identical failure only, or never.
Job asks: job 1 'Motor noise buries the Morse from the roof.'; job 2 keep 'The dome motor whines at 4 kHz; the 12 V shutter latch shares the line.'; job 3 'A new beacon: 100 MHz, vertically polarised.' Optionally point at the gallery: give the RADIO exhibit a brass '100 MHz' tag that pulses when job 3 starts.
Extend logic.test.ts:298 with /λ\/4 ≈|reroute|move the|fit and orient/i, and add a test over JOBS[].ask.
findings.verify: Unit test passes with the stricter regex. Shot after a wrong-rod LOG: the toast has no number that equals a rack label.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced: a wrong-rod LOG gives 'A 1.5 m whip is far from a quarter wave at 100 MHz (λ = c/f = 3.0 m, so λ/4 ≈ 0.75 m)' (v1.mjs output; logic.ts:162-164). The rack carries a '75 cm' label, so one failure gives the answer away. The job asks name the methods (logic.ts:122, :126; panel text in v1.mjs output), against DR-39. The test that would catch this is at logic.test.ts:102-105, not 296-299; its regex only checks /Pick a|move the motor|reroute|filter harder|Stand the rod/ and only over problems[], never over JOBS[].ask.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/v1.mjs console: 'toast fail The decode fails: A 1.5 m whip is far from a quarter wave at 100 MHz (λ = c/f = 3.0 m, so λ/4 ≈ 0.75 m)'
findings.fix_correction: Extend the test at logic.test.ts:104, not :298.

findings.title: The decoder readout and the verdict disagree: 'Decodes' is shown while 40–50 % of the characters are junk, and the win screen ends on a garbled message
findings.problem:
decoded() garbles each character with probability (12 − S/N)/12 (logic.ts:247-248). judge() says 'Decodes' from 6 dB (logic.ts:172-176). So at 7.1 dB the toast says '“DOME OPEN” · Decodes', while the scope's decode line shows about 41 % junk. At 6 dB, half the characters are junk.
In the shortcut run, the final win frame shows the scope reading '%TAR% ?LE?R' with the confetti (shot 17). The payoff message is unreadable at the moment of victory, contradicting the 'Decodes' verdict and the success sound.
The player can't tell which to believe, the readout or the toast. That muddies the threshold idea (S/N decides whether a message gets through), which is the core concept of the room.
findings.fix:
Make the readout follow the same thresholds. In logic.ts decoded(): bad = snr ≥ reliableSnr ? 0 : snr ≥ decodeSnr ? 0.12*(reliableSnr−snr)/(reliableSnr−decodeSnr) : 0.5 + 0.5*min(1,(decodeSnr−snr)/12). That gives a clean message above 12 dB, an occasional single flicker between 6 and 12 dB, and mostly junk below 6 dB.
After a successful LOG, freeze the decode line on the logged message for that job: store `this.logged[i].message` and draw it in green on the scope until the next job's first change.
findings.verify: Unit tests: decoded('STARS CLEAR',7,e) has ≤ 2 junk characters over 20 epochs, and decoded(…,3,e) has ≥ 5. Re-run b.mjs: the win shot shows 'STARS CLEAR'.
findings.verify_reason: decoded() garbles with bad = (12−snr)/12 (logic.ts:248). I measured the junk fraction over 50 epochs: 51 % at 6 dB, 41 % at 7.1 dB, 12 % at 10.7 dB, while judge() says 'Decodes' from 6 dB. My win frame shows 'S#%R# %LEAR' on the scope under the confetti (verify-observatory-teach-05-win-push.jpg, -06), so the payoff message is unreadable at the moment of victory.

findings.title: Switch-on captions are physically wrong in two setups, and the documented 'resonance makes the whine louder' moment never happens on the intended path
findings.problem:
(1) stepCaption() for any series coil says '…It ramps up (ringing as the capacitor charges), then carries steady DC to the latch' (station.ts:207). It says this even when there is no capacitor, or the shunt part is a coil. With series L + shunt L the latch gets 0.39 V (computed), not 'steady DC to the latch'. stepShort() (station.ts:214) says the same.
(2) With the job-1 capacitor carried over, 1 mH + 1.5 µF, the circuit is over-damped: Z0 = √(L/C) ≈ 26 Ω against a 50 Ω source. Step peak 11.04 V equals the final value (no overshoot), and the filter's maximum gain is 0.99 (no peak). Shot 29 shows a smooth latch-voltage rise, yet the toast says 'ringing'.
(3) The spec comment (tests/station-observatory.spec.ts:146) and PROGRESS.md:333-335 claim 'At 1 mH the coil and capacitor ring near 4 kHz and make the whine louder, which the spectrum shows'. In the model, 1 mH + 1.5 µF cuts 4 kHz by 5.4 dB; it is quieter, not louder. The resonant boost only appears for small C, for example 10 mH + 150 nF: +4.2 dB at 3.8 kHz (n3.mjs). A player arriving from job 1 never sees the advertised lesson.
(4) The step toast is not refreshed when parts change. Shot 28 shows the series-C caption still up while a coil sits in the slot.
(5) The same caption appears on the scope and in the toast at once (shot 26; DR-41).
findings.verify: Unit tests: stepCaption for {series:L1m, shunt:C1u5} does not contain 'ring'; for {series:L10m, shunt:L1m} it mentions that the latch gets no DC. Retake shot 28 after the change: no stale toast.
findings.verify_reason: Checked in code and numbers. stepCaption() says 'ringing as the capacitor charges' for any series L (station.ts:207). 1 mH + 1.5 µF has a step peak of 11.04 V equal to its final value (no ring), a maximum gain of 0.996 and −5.4 dB at 4 kHz (num.mjs), yet the toast says 'ringing' (observatory-teach-29 shows the smooth rise). Series L + shunt L gives 0.39 V at the latch. The spec comment claiming '1 mH rings near 4 kHz and makes the whine louder' is real, but it is at tests/station-observatory.spec.ts:35 (the file has 74 lines, not 146); PROGRESS.md:335 says the same. A stale series-C toast is visible with a coil slotted (observatory-teach-28), and the caption appears twice in shot 26 (the toast's long form and the scope's short form). One error in the fix: 1 mH + 100 nF peaks at 14.6 kHz, not 4–5 kHz; only 10 mH + 100 nF peaks near 4.6 kHz (+3.6 dB).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/num.mjs: '1m1u5 maxgain 0.996 … g4k dB -5.37 step peak 11.04 final 11.04', 'LL latch 0.39', '10m150n peak 1.623 3854'
findings.fix_correction: Fix tests/station-observatory.spec.ts:35 (not :146). For a real resonance moment, use 10 mH + 100 nF (peak about 4.6 kHz) or 10 mH + 150 nF (about 3.9 kHz); 1 mH + 100 nF peaks at about 15 kHz and does not boost the 4 kHz whine.

findings.title: Free, live trial and error plus an oracle prompt: 'Enter · Log the decode' appears exactly when the setup is reliable, so knobs and rods can be swept without reasoning
findings.problem:
Measuring is free and live, which is good (R4A asked for it). The scope spectrum and S/N update as the knob turns. But prompt() switches to 'Enter · Log the decode' exactly when S/N ≥ 12, the tone ≥ 50 %, the latch is OK and the antenna is right (station.ts:377; shots 22, 30). The panel rows also flip to green or red per threshold (station.ts:357-360).
So the winning procedure is to press → until the pill changes. In job 3 there are 4 rods × 2 orientations at no cost, with the panel's 'Antenna' row turning green on the right one. The player can reach 'Elegant' in every job with no idea of corner frequency or λ/4 (DR-38). Sweeping a knob while watching the spectrum is real learning, so keep that. The oracle prompt and the per-row ticks are what replace reasoning with pattern matching.
findings.fix:
Make the prompt neutral: always show 'Enter · Log the decode' once any can is slotted or the route has changed. Remove the green/red ok-class from the 'Signal/noise' and 'Antenna' panel rows (station.ts:358-359) and let the scope's S/N colour and the audible Morse carry the judgement.
For job 3, replace the instant 'Antenna' tick with a continuous beacon bleep that grows with antennaFactor (an audio gain proportional to ant), so the right rod is found by ear. Still add one sentence of world reference: pulse the RADIO exhibit's '100 MHz' plaque.
findings.verify: Spec: with a tier-0 setup the prompt still reads 'Log the decode'. Shot: no green tick on the S/N row in tier 0 or tier 3.
findings.verify_reason: prompt() returns 'Enter · Log the decode' only when S/N ≥ 12, tone ≥ 50 %, the latch holds and the antenna is OK (station.ts:377). Shot 30 (12.2 dB) shows 'Log the decode' and shot 29 (2.0 dB) shows 'Turn the knob'. Panel rows take ok classes per threshold (station.ts:357-360). Rods and orientation are free to cycle, and DR-38 asks that brute-force cycling costs credits. This is a design-quality concern, correctly rated P2.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/observatory-teach-29-step-L1m.jpg vs observatory-teach-30-step-L10m-C1u.jpg (prompt pill flips exactly at reliable)

findings.title: The filter name in the panel is wrong for series C + shunt C: it is called 'high-pass', but it is a band-pass
findings.problem: describe() returns 'high-pass (series C)' whenever the series part is a capacitor, ignoring the shunt part (logic.ts:150-155). With series 1 µF and shunt 1.5 µF, the panel reads 'Filter: high-pass (series C)' while the tags show '↑245 Hz' and '↓2.3 kHz' (shot 25). That circuit is a band-pass: high-pass at 245 Hz, low-pass at 2.3 kHz. Its curve on the scope (shot 25) is a hump, which contradicts the label. Similarly, series L + shunt L shows the generic 'filter', and series R + shunt L shows 'high-pass (shunt L)', which is acceptable.
findings.fix: In describe(), add: s C + p C → 'band-pass (series C + shunt C)'; s L + p L → 'band-pass (series L + shunt L)'; s C + p L → 'high-pass (2-part)'; s R + p L → 'high-pass (RL)'. Add a unit test per pair.
findings.verify: Unit test: filterName({series:C1u,shunt:C1u5}) matches /band-pass/. Retake shot 25.
findings.verify_reason: describe() returns 'high-pass (series C)' for any series C (logic.ts:153); filterName({series:C1µ, shunt:C1.5µ}) gives 'high-pass (series C)' (num.mjs), and shot 25 shows the hump-shaped curve. One sub-claim is wrong: series L + shunt L returns 'high-pass (shunt L)', not the generic 'filter' (num.mjs: 'LL high-pass (shunt L)'). That label is also wrong, since series L low-pass + shunt L high-pass is band-pass-like, so the fix's band-pass entry for L+L is right.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/num.mjs: 'name CC high-pass (series C) LL high-pass (shunt L)'

findings.title: Meaningless readings: 'S/N −180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%' with the TONE ● indicator lit, after the gust or with a 3.1 cm whip
findings.problem:
dB() clamps to 1e-9 (logic.ts:85). With the default 3.1 cm whip in job 3 the antenna factor is 0.000, so the scope and panel print 'S/N -180.0 dB' and 'Tone level 0%' (shot 13). That reads as a bug and teaches nothing about scale.
At the same time the scope's 'TONE ●' marker keeps blinking with the Morse key timing (station.ts:250, :255), as if a tone were arriving, while the trace shows only filtered noise. A learner sees 'tone on' plus 0 % tone and can't reconcile them.
findings.fix: Clamp the displayed S/N to '< −30 dB'. When r.level < 0.05, print 'no signal' in red instead of a number, on both the panel row and the scope line. Draw TONE ● only when on && r.tones[0].after > 0.1; otherwise 'TONE —'.
findings.verify: Shot at job 3 start: the panel shows 'no signal', there is no −180, and TONE shows the dash.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced at the start of job 3 (3.1 cm whip, flat): the panel and scope read 'S/N -180.0 dB', 'Tone level 0%', and the scope shows 'TONE ●' (verify-observatory-teach-04-job3-start-r3.jpg). The antenna factor is 1e-36, and dB() clamps at 1e-9 (logic.ts:85). The TONE marker follows Morse key timing only (station.ts:250, :255).

findings.title: Job 1 introduces four new ideas at once, and the elegant tier changes with where the cart was dropped (with a wrong 'Cheaper parts' note)
findings.problem:
(1) Job 1 asks the player to meet, all at once: noise falls with distance (the cart), coupling depends on routing (the lever), series vs shunt topology, and a shunt C setting a low-pass corner frequency. That is four new ideas in the first job (DR-27 allows at most two).
(2) The 'cheapest' target is recomputed from the cart's distance at log time (logic.ts:177-179). If Pip carries the cart 10 m or more away (the room allows up to about 17 m), 'no cans + reroute' becomes the elegant answer (n2/numbers output: d=10 gives 12.7 dB with no filter). The taught 1 µF shunt then drops to tier 2 with the note 'Reliable. Cheaper parts can do it too (cost 0 vs 1)'. 'Cheaper parts' when the answer is no parts is wrong wording, and the bonus 'Elegant: the leanest filter each time' is lost for doing the lesson well.
findings.fix:
Split job 1 into two beats. Beat 1a: move the cart; the scope alone shows the noise falling, with no filter needed to log (tier 2 when ≥ 12 dB, rerouting optional). Beat 1b: a second noise source the player cannot move (the dome motor, see the shutter finding) needs the shunt-C filter.
In judge(), cap the distance used for `best` at CART_SAFE (use CART_SAFE, not max(distance, CART_SAFE)), so the elegant target is stable. When best.cost===0, write 'A cleaner setup needs no cans at all here'.
findings.verify: Unit test: judge(garble, {cartDistance:14, shunt:C1u, rerouted:true}).tier===3. Teaching table in the review: one or two new ideas per job.
findings.verify_reason: Part (2) is verified numerically. At cart distance 10, 12 or 14 m with the route flipped, the cheapest is 'no cans, cable rerouted' at cost 0. The taught 1 µF shunt drops to tier 2 with 'Reliable. Cheaper parts can do it too (cost 0 vs 1)' (logic.ts:178-179). The room is 22×16 (levels/observatory.ts:22), so 10+ m from RX (-3.25,-2.45) is reachable. Part (1), 'four ideas', is a judgement call against DR-27. Distance and routing are arguably one coupling idea, but even counted that way job 1 adds both coupling and the shunt-C corner, so 'more than one' holds.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/num.mjs: 'j1 d 10 1uF+rr tier 2 Reliable. Cheaper parts can do it too (cost 0 vs 1).  cheapest no cans, cable rerouted 0'

findings.title: Spectrum gallery: invisible bands painted in rainbow false colour without a label, 'f ≈ 30000 GHz', and wall sentences; the exhibits are passive and never tied to the bench
findings.problem:
(1) BANDS (room.ts:31-39) colour the panels RADIO red, MICROWAVE orange, INFRARED amber, VISIBLE green, UV violet, X-RAY blue, GAMMA dark (shots 36, 37). Mapping radio to red suggests that radio is 'red light', which is the misconception DR-35 names. There is no 'false colour' caption.
(2) freqText uses SI prefixes only up to G below 1e14 Hz (room.ts:40-43), so INFRARED prints 'f ≈ 30000 GHz' instead of '30 THz' (shot 36).
(3) The header 'THE SPECTRUM: ONE WAVE, c = f × λ' and the 12-word warning strip are sentences on the wall (room.ts:91-92; DR-49).
(4) The gallery holds the clue for job 3 (RADIO: λ ≈ 3 m, f ≈ 100 MHz), but nothing points the player to it, so the exhibit teaches by reading only (DR-26).
findings.fix:
Give the six non-visible headers a neutral slate (#4a4e66) with a small 'false colour' corner tag. Only VISIBLE keeps a rainbow strip.
Add 'T' and 'P' to the prefix list in si() (room.ts:40), giving [1e15,'P'],[1e12,'T'].
Shorten the header to 'c = f × λ' and the warning to an icon row (☢ on UV, X-ray and gamma panels, already partly there via the tags).
When job 3 starts, light the RADIO panel with a lamp pulse (pointLamp intensity 4 for 3 s) so the gallery becomes the reference the player walks to.
findings.verify: Gallery crop: INFRARED reads '30 THz'; non-visible headers are neutral; a false-colour tag is present. Job-3 start shot shows the RADIO panel lit.
findings.verify_reason: INFRARED prints 'f ≈ 30000 GHz' (verify-observatory-teach-06 and -05, visible on the gallery). This is because freqText only switches to powers of ten at ≥1e14 and si() stops at G (room.ts:40-43). The band headers use hues (RADIO red #e5484d etc., room.ts:31-39) with no false-colour label, which breaks DR-35. The header and warning strip are sentences (room.ts:91-92). Nothing links RADIO to job 3. Adding only [1e12,'T'] is enough; 'P' is never reached because freqText already handles ≥1e14.
findings.fix_correction: Adding [1e12,'T'] to si() is sufficient; 'P' is unreachable because freqText switches to ×10ⁿ at ≥1e14.

findings.title: The 'game tuning values' disclosure is hidden during play, and the bench whips are not to scale with no on-screen note
findings.problem:
The panel line 'Decoder: S/N ≥ 6 dB decodes, ≥ 12 dB is reliable; latch needs ≥ 9 V. Game tuning values.' (station.ts:361) has `display:none` unless the game is paused (src/ui/ui.css:226-228). It was absent from every bench shot (07, 22, 30).
The rack whips are drawn at 0.1 + 0.34·length (station.ts:55-56): the 1.5 m whip is 0.61 m and the 3.1 cm whip is 0.11 m, yet each is labelled with its real length (shot 34). Nothing on screen says 'not to scale'.
The 6 dB, 12 dB and 9 V thresholds, and the −6 dB reroute, are tuning values that a learner will take as rules of thumb (DR-32).
findings.fix: Show a 2-word chip on the scope bezel, 'tuned values', with the full line on hover or in pause. Add a tiny 'not to scale' plaque on the rod rack (sign() at rack z .2, 10 mm text).
findings.verify: Bench shot shows the chip and the plaque; text height ≥ 14 px or legible in a crop.
findings.verify_reason: ui.css:226-228 sets .station-panel .profile to display:none unless body[data-paused]. The text is in station.ts:361. It is absent from every bench shot (07, 30, verify-04). rodLen = .1 + .34·length (station.ts:55-56); only a code comment says 'not to scale', and nothing shows on screen. This breaks DR-32.

findings.title: The gust that knocks the whip flat happens indoors on the bench, and its dust reads as snowballs; the polarisation cause is not readable
findings.problem:
After job 2, gust() sets vertical=false and bursts 8 'dust' puffs at the bench mount (station.ts:199, :205). On screen these are 3–4 big white spheres sitting over the ANTENNA (shot 32). The bench is indoors and the whip flips toward the camera, so it is hard to see that it is now flat (only the crop, shot 34, shows it sideways).
The 'roof gust' story conflicts with the room: the real mast is on the receiver rack (room.ts:84-85), while the bench has its own whip. The player has two antennas, one inert, and can't tell which one the beacon reaches. Polarisation is meant to be 'found by accident' (R4A), but here it is just a state change with no visible cause.
findings.fix: Move the whip mount to the rack's mast top (the real roof antenna) and keep the bench rack as the spare-whip store, or say the bench mount is the 'roof feed'. Play the gust on the mast: tilt animation over 0.4 s, a few thin streak particles (the 'spark' style with a pale colour) instead of puffs, and a rattling sound. Lay the bench whip along x (sideways to the camera), not along z.
findings.verify: Shot at +0.1 s and +0.6 s after job 2's log: the whip is visibly tipping sideways; no white balls.
findings.verify_reason: gust() bursts 8 'dust' puffs at the bench mount (station.ts:205). observatory-teach-32 shows three large white spheres over the ANTENNA mount. The flattened whip rotates around z (station.ts:235), and at the bench camera it is hard to read as flat. The real mast stands on the rack (room.ts:84-85) and is inert, so there are two antennas. I did not retake the +0.6 s shot; I relied on the reviewer's 32 and 34.

findings.title: Bench text load and duplicated values: about 70 words on screen, S/N shown twice, a step caption in two places, and the wording mismatch 'Roll the cart' vs 'Grab the cart'
findings.problem:
At the bench the player sees the job card, a 3-line ask, a 9-row panel, the scope with its own S/N, the decode, legend words and frequency ticks, a two-line toast, and the prompt pill. That is about 70 words outside the monitor (shots 07, 25, 30; DR-40 says ~25).
S/N and the per-part corners appear on both the scope and the panel (DR-41), and step captions appear on the scope and in the toast at once (shot 26).
In the room, the card says 'Roll the noisy motor cart away…' while the prompt says 'Grab the cart' (station.ts:85; objectives.ts:83 fallback; shot 03). Pip then lifts the cart to chest height and carries it (shot 05); nothing rolls.
The '1.5 m' rack label is overlapped by the red route-lever knob in the 'past motor' state (shot 07, '1.5 r').
findings.fix:
Panel: keep only Series, Shunt, Latch V and Parts cost. Drop Filter, Tone level, Signal/noise (the scope shows them), Motor cart and Cable (the room shows them). Remove the ask paragraph once the first can is slotted.
In ObservatoryBench.prompt(false), return {key:'E', text:'Push the motor cart away'} when Pip is within 1.6 m of the cart, and rename step 1 to 'Move the noisy motor cart away from the receiver'.
Shift the route lever group (station.ts:132) to x −1.32, z .44 so it clears the 1.5 m tag.
findings.verify: Word count in a bench shot ≤ 35 outside the scope. Shot at the cart: the card and the prompt use the same verb. Shot 07 retake: the '1.5 m' label is clear.
findings.verify_reason: The card reads 'Roll the noisy motor cart away…' while the prompt reads 'E · Grab the cart' (observatory-teach-42; objectives.ts nearest() fallback). Pip then carries it, and the prompt becomes 'Keep rolling it away' / 'Set the cart down' (v1.mjs output, observatory-teach-05). S/N appears on the scope and the panel at once (shot 07), which breaks DR-41. The red lever knob covers the '1.5 m' rack label in the PAST MOTOR state ('1.5 r' in observatory-teach-07). I did not count the ~70 words exactly, but the panel, ask, scope and toast together clearly exceed 25. One problem with the fix: prompting 'Push the motor cart away' while the mechanic is a carry swaps one mismatch for another.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-observatory-teach/v1.mjs console: 'prompt carrying E | Keep rolling it away'
src/stations/observatory/station.ts:366 ('Keep rolling it away' while carried)
findings.fix_correction: Use one verb that matches the mechanic. Pip lifts and carries the cart, so step 1 should read 'Move/Carry the noisy motor cart away from the receiver', station.ts:366 should read 'Keep carrying it away', and the cart's grab prompt can stay 'Grab the cart'. Do not introduce 'Push' unless the cart is made a push-only heavy prop.

notes.teaching: The model underneath is honest and better than any other station I have read. It is a true complex transfer function with a 50 Ω source and a 600 Ω load (logic.ts:76-82). The coils have winding resistance. A series C really blocks DC (latch 0 V). A shunt L really shorts it (0.39 V). A series R really divides the 12 V (470 Ω leaves 6.4 V), and the toast names that number. The quarter-wave arithmetic is right (100 MHz → 0.75 m), and so is the ~20 dB cross-polarisation penalty. The E6 knob values are real. The live before/after spectrum with the |H(f)| curve, the corner lines sweeping as the knob turns, and the Morse audio are the best 'concept is the mechanic' feedback in the game. Carrying the noisy cart away and hearing the scope clean up is a genuine physical lesson. The real problems are in gating and wording, not in the physics. (1) Tier 1 'Decodes' advances every job, so the room can be finished without a filter in job 1 and with one capacitor in job 2. The LC idea and the DC-latch idea are then never met, and that run still grades A/A/A. (2) The per-part corner tags mislead in the LC pair (the coil reads '11 kHz' while the filter acts at 1.6 kHz). (3) Some captions are false: 'ringing' when the circuit is over-damped, and 'steady DC to the latch' with a shunt coil. The 'resonance makes it louder' moment described in PROGRESS and the spec never happens on the intended path. (4) The antenna failure prints 0.75 m. (5) Cable routing, the room's spatial idea, is a bench lever with no room cable. Truthfulness at the level taught is mostly good. The things that would mislead are the filter label (series C + shunt C called 'high-pass', which is a band-pass), the reroute working regardless of where the motor is, and the rainbow false colour on the spectrum gallery.
notes.clarity: The bench is legible at a glance: board topology (RECEIVER → SERIES → node with SHUNT to GROUND → DECODER/LATCH), clear can icons, a big scope, and the S/N coloured by threshold. Clarity breaks in five places. (1) Text load: about 70 words, with S/N duplicated on the scope and panel, and step captions both on the screen and in a toast. (2) The value tags' corner line is about 6 px, unreadable. (3) The decoder readout shows heavy junk while the toast says 'Decodes'; the win shot can end on '%TAR% ?LE?R'. (4) Absurd numbers (−180 dB) and a TONE ● lit with 0 % tone. (5) The latch job refers to a 'shutter' and a 'dome motor' that have no model in the world. The in-room flow is clear: the marker sits on the cart, the card and prompt agree on the target (only the verb differs), and the bench marker follows.
notes.fun: Rolling the cart away and hearing the buzz drop is a nice physical beat. Sweeping a knob while the corner line glides across the spectrum and the Morse comes clean is a satisfying toy. The rest is sitting at a desk clicking. There is no chaos route or physical consequence: the latch failing slams nothing, the dome never opens, and the win camera misses the dome light-up. The cable, the game's star, is unused in the one room whose lesson is cable routing. Building the shutter and the room receiver cable would turn the two best ideas (DC must reach the latch; keep the line away from the motor) into physical comedy.
notes.playability: Every scripted path ran with zero console errors across four scripts. Cart pickup, carry and drop work. The bench acts, knob drag/arrows, and Esc to stand up work. The job advances correctly, the gust flips the whip, and logging tiers work. There were no soft-locks: a failed LOG just costs a mistake and you keep tinkering. Minor issues: the route lever overlaps the '1.5 m' rack tag, and the step toast goes stale after a part swap.
notes.models: (Not my dimension; noted in passing.) The bench reads as a proper toy workstation. The filter cans have distinct component tops (banded resistor, copper coil, capacitor can). The receiver rack has a plaque and mast. The dome has no shutter or motor. There is no cable linking the rack to the bench; the bench lead starts in mid-air at the desk edge. The gust dust reads as white balls.

rechecked: R4A 'orientation starts upright, so polarisation never comes up': FIXED. gust() flips the whip flat at the start of job 3 (station.ts:199,205; shots 32, 34). Its readability is still weak (P2 finding).

R4A 'prompts give it away (swap the part that blocks DC; λ/4 = c ÷ f ÷ 4)': PARTIAL / REGRESSED into toasts. The prompts are clean (station.ts:363-379), but the antenna failure toast prints λ/4 ≈ 0.75 m (logic.ts:163) and the job asks list methods (logic.ts:122,126).

R4A 'values can't be reasoned about; brute-force ~42 combos': PARTIAL. There are now E6 knobs with corner tags and spectrum lines, but the tags are unreadable and mislead in an LC pair, and the oracle prompt lets the player sweep without reasoning.
R4A 'job 3 is one click': FIXED to two clicks (rod + orient). The filter still carries over from job 2.
R4A / NEXT_STEPS §1 'cable routing is a bench lever; make the receiver line the real room cable': STILL OPEN. There is no room cable (shot 42), and the lever works regardless of the motor's position.
R4A 'tone level and S/N are two separate pass bars': STILL OPEN (both panel rows), now also mismatched with the decoder readout.
R4A cross-cutting 'experiments graded as damage': mostly FIXED here. Live readings are free; only a failed LOG counts. Damage limit 1.
R3A N9 rod captions hidden by the rods: FIXED (captions moved in front). New overlap: the route lever ball covers the '1.5 m' tag in the 'past motor' state (shot 07).
R3A N9 rerouted cable across the ANTENNA plate: FIXED. The clear spline goes behind the mount (shot 11).
R3A N1 first prompt 'Grab the chair': FIXED. There is no prompt at spawn; 'Grab the cart' at the cart (shot 03), though the verb differs from the card's 'Roll'.
PROGRESS claim 'Job 2: no single part at any value decodes reliably': true only for the 12 dB reliable bar (best single C 11.9 dB); single caps still pass the 6 dB decode bar and advance the job.
PROGRESS / spec claim 'At 1 mH the LC rings near 4 kHz and makes the whine louder': NOT TRUE in the model for 1 mH + 1.5 µF (−5.4 dB at 4 kHz, no peak, no overshoot).
